Ford’s S650 Mustang Becomes a Lot More Practical in Fantasy Land With New Wagon Body Style
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
The seventh-generation Ford Mustang blew three candles off its birthday cake earlier this year, and just for kicks, we will remind you that it is the only muscle car in production to feature a V8 engine.
Actually, it boasts not just one but quit a few V8 powertrains, and even more if we start bringing the Shelby versions into discussion. And that’s something that has given Dodge a headache, as its electric and six-pot bet on the modern-day Charger hasn’t exactly paid off. Therefore, the Stellantis-owned brand is now considering a V8-powered version of the Charger. Moreover, the next-gen Chevy Camaro is also expected to launch with V8 power, though instead of a regular coupe body style, it might be offered solely as a four-door sedan.
That may not sound like a wise choice at first, but let’s not forget that the modern Dodge Charger is also offered as a four-door sedan, and if the bowtie company indeed goes down this route, then it will eventually force Ford’s hand to launch a similar version of the Mustang. And to be honest, that’s not a huge eyebrow-raiser, because such a thing has been rumored several times over the years. However, could the Blue Oval go beyond the traditional sedan and launch a station wagon variant of its pony car?
The answer to this question is obviously “no.” Nothing suggests that the Dearborn company plans to turn the S650 (or its successor that should still be a few good years away, as there’s no reason to believe that the ‘Stang won’t survive for the next generation) into an estate. Such a thing would be a very practical family car, and a low-riding alternative to traditional crossovers and SUVs, and between us, it would not be bad at all. That’s my opinion, anyway, and before asking you to reveal yours, we will delve into it.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik And by “it,” we mean the five-door version of the S650 Ford Mustang that was rendered by @kelsonik and shared on social media recently. This thing retains the traditional design of the pony car at the front. Further back, it has a longer roofline that is arched toward the rear. It also features four instead of two doors, and the front ones are shorter. Out back, it sports the same design overall, albeit with a tailgate rather than a trunk lid, complete with a large spoiler attached to it, and a windscreen wiper.
The tailgate opens up into a very generous cargo area that could easily eat a few large suitcases, thus making this model the perfect car for a week-long getaway. The space between the axles has also been enlarged, thus translating to more legroom for the backseat occupants, though the headroom for those sitting at the rear does not seem to be very good. Another interesting novelty is the frameless design of the side windows, which makes this model look a lot sportier.
The car sits a bit closer to the ground than usual, has some skirts on the lower parts of the body all around, and rides on wheels that seem to be brand new. The alloys are concave, larger than the OEM ones, and feature a Y-spoke design. The sport a black finish in these CGIs, and they’re joined by other black elements on the outside. The rest of the car has a red look, and the interior is home to black leather upholstery, as far as we can see.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik It looks like the quoted rendering artist has imagined the Ford Mustang Wagon in the Dark Horse SC configuration. This is the range-topping version of the brand’s pony car, in case you forgot, and it is pretty much the modern-day equivalent of the S550-based Shelby GT500. It packs a 5.2-liter supercharged V8 engine, and has 795 horsepower (806 ps/593 kW) and 660 lb-ft (895 Nm) of torque available via the right pedal, delivered to the rear axle through a Tremec 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
That’s a healthy jump over the older Ford Mustang Shelby GT500, which had 760 hp (771 ps/567 kW) and 627 lb-ft (847 Nm) of torque on tap. This model hit 60 mph (97 kph) in a little over three seconds, and the modern-day Mustang Dark Horse SC is estimated to complete the sprint in less than three seconds, running the standing quarter mile in 10.8 seconds, as per third-party estimates.
Naturally, a station wagon version of this model would be a bit slower due to the extra weight, and would need proper chassis calibration if it wants to win more hearts. But as mentioned above, we would not hold our breath for such a thing, as it won’t happen. A Ford Mustang Sedan, on the other hand, seems quite possible. If you had to choose between a four-door and a five-door version of the S650 Mustang, which one would you get and why? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
